state: We need a recovery design for emails announcing a physical item in a Can mailroom draft. There is no implemented runtime, and this exercise changes neither fees nor carrier handling. Current policy demands location-authorized staff, a currently verified intended recipient, retained failure/uncertainty and idempotent retries. Email's declared capability has one send operation and no application-facing reconciliation method. Background retries of an admitted intent reuse its key and frozen recipient/content; another send statement admits a distinct key. Protected delivery observations contain status, identity, result and error only, leaving the original request inaccessible to source. Unknown delivery may already have reached the provider, and failed can be a malformed result after a completed remote send. Error classifications/messages therefore cannot justify safe repetition. Skipped signifies an intent that was not dispatched once cancelled, superseded or ineligible. Provider success does not show reading or collection. Today the item selects its latest receipt; a success callback for that association may mark received as notified but cannot finish custody. New collection notices are forbidden after collection, forward preparation or return, while service expiration alone leaves held-property resolution available. Hold the following measures equal across options involving an additional send: immutable staff-only storage of the previous receipt and exact account, email address, subject and body; checks of current staff/location rights, current contact/account/address, held-item eligibility and latest association, repeated when dispatching; attributable nonblank reason; unchanged scheduled-reminder accounting; no recovery replacement for pending or already succeeded receipts; replay deduplication for the requesting operation. Existing receipt success can also be applied to repair a missed business-state callback without an external lookup. Human assertions cannot create a verified non-delivery fact, and a new status-query capability is not assumed. Weigh only the remaining business recovery choice after ordinary bounded delivery retry. No live provider call or implementation is requested.

recovery_policy.instructions: Recommend one approach for the next full Can/JavaScript design witness. Compare recovery usefulness, explicit uncertainty, simplicity, duplicate-message exposure and what is possible without a provider reconciliation call. Your answer is advice, not adoption or execution proof.

criteria.runtime_only: Keep recovery within background retries of the existing delivery, with app visibility and a repair action for known success. Do not initiate another message from failed, unknown or skipped states. This avoids a new domain resend workflow, but operators cannot resolve an exhausted or ambiguous send from the business app until a suitable operational/provider facility exists.
criteria.evidenced_resend: Gate an additional send of the stored request on an attributed staff report of a provider investigation establishing nonacceptance; an undispatched skipped attempt instead needs a reason alone. Retain the previous outcome and check it again. This favors documented external checking over quick replacement, adds a manual evidence step, cannot authenticate the report merely by storing it, and leaves evidence-less outages unresolved.
criteria.acknowledged_resend: Permit a new delivery of the retained request when current authorized staff supplies a reason and knowingly allows a possible duplicate for failed/unknown outcomes; require just a reason for skipped. Keep the ambiguous predecessor visible without changing it. This supplies practical recovery using existing constructs and explicit accountability, but accepts repeat-email risk and the cost of an immutable notice record; it makes no assertion that the earlier transport was retried or its uncertainty removed.
